A Collective Bargain Notes Read after Confessions of a Union Buster . Interesting details on the L.A. Teachers' union . Specifically giving up pay for more green spaces for kids, combats arguments that teachers unions are greedy. Talks about how higher paid/skilled teachers are fired to avoid paying benefits and high turnover. Also talks about nursing. Some nurses being turned against each other by union busters. Also talks about the strategy of bringing in established unions and their representatives to start one's own union. Includes union busting tactics at the end of the book.

Recommended this book to a friend's dad, who didn't get through the first chapter because of the impending rape, which is frustrating because the rapists are all immediately gruesomely killed before they can do anything in the page after he quit. It's nice how averse he was to it, though.

docs.text: Confessions of a Union Buster Notes Super interesting book! Used as inspiration for a writing project. Some tactics he mentioned: Divide and Conquer: Highlight differences of interest between groups of workers. Men vs women, day shift vs night shift, young vs old, etc. Fixing some problems on behalf of management: Getting rid of core gripes to take steam away from the workers and make it clear that management is capable of solving problems without the union. Choosing mouthpieces from management: Since managers are barred from union membership, they can be held in specific anti-union training. Selecting for well-respected and senior staff, potentially dangling promotion or turning workers against each other. Walking the floor: One of the first steps, getting a feel for the office and pin-pointing popular workers and potential tensions. Captive Audience Meetings: Mandatory anti-union meetings for workers. Barrage of emails: Blowing union powers/information privileges to fear monger (EX: The union has a list of all of your emails and addresses!)

docs.text: Dangerous Games Notes The first half of Dangerous Games gives a history of roleplaying games and the Satanic Panic through its emergence in 1979-1982, its peak in 1982-1991, and its shifting focus amidst the super-predator craze of 1991-2001. The second half breaks down the purpose of play, reasons why the Christian Right fears imaginary worldbuilding, and how they engage in it anyway. It looks at religion as a roleplaying game and roleplaying games as religion. I was given this book for Christmas many years ago, but it sat on my desk. When I did a research project on Theophilus Riesinger , the priest who performed the infamous 1928 Earling Exorcism , I found references to a secret 1934 primary account that had been banned from publication by the Catholic Church. There were two original copies locked away in university libraries that weren't available online. I discovered a book chapter covering the document on an academic journals website and saw the author allowed PDF requests. I emailed him in a haze at 3 in the morning and only afterwards, when checking his website, did I realize he was Joseph Laycock, author of Dangerous Games. The book was sitting right in front of me on my desk at the time, unread. The next morning, Laycock emailed me back with a a 34-page PDF of his original scans of the lost texts from the university libraries- way more than I bargained for! This incident is why Joseph Laycock is my favorite author ever and also my best friend. Source Bugs's Bookshelf

docs.text: Debt: The First 5,000 Years Notes I was a big fan of The Dawn of Everything and wanted to read more David Graeber. This book spawned a fascination with wanting to plan a DnD setting and campaign focused around Debt. I really enjoy the individual anthropological case studies about how different cultures interact with Debt. I have a bunch of old notes I want to dig up and paste on this page. Specifically, the anecdote about the IMF and Malaria really hooked me from the beginning and made me question my belief in the truthism that People ought to repay their debts . This book motivated me to read Margaret Attwood's Payback . I feel like it also made me think about Homewreckers in a new light.

docs.text: Homewreckers Notes This rivals The Israel Lobby and U.S. Foreign Policy for the book I am most frustrated about not being able to recall most of. For that reason, I have gone back through a summary of this one to take my notes again. The book investigates how Wall Street investors, banks, private equity firms, and government officials profited from the 2008 Financial Crisis and the subsequent foreclosure epidemic. Its central argument is that the crisis was not simply the result of irresponsible borrowers or an unavoidable market collapse. Government policies and financial institutions helped create the conditions for mass foreclosure, then enabled wealthy investors to acquire distressed homes at enormous discounts. A particularly important thread is the emergence of large corporate landlords and the connection between the foreclosure crisis and the political rise of Donald Trump . Key organizations and vocabulary Mortgage-Backed Securities ( MBS ) — Financial products created by bundling mortgages and selling claims on their payments to investors. Collateralized Debt Obligations ( CDOs ) — Structured financial products that can repackage mortgage-related debts into different risk categories. Underwater Mortgage — A mortgage whose outstanding balance exceeds the home's market value. TARP — Troubled Asset Relief Program, the 2008 federal financial rescue program. HAMP — Home Affordable Modification Program, designed to help struggling homeowners obtain mortgage modifications. Private Equity — Investment firms that acquire and manage assets using pooled capital. Single-Family Rental ( SFR ) — Houses owned and rented out, increasingly as a large-scale institutional investment. People Steve Mnuchin - Former Goldman Sachs executive. - Led an investor group that purchased failed mortgage lender IndyMac from the government in 2009. - Renamed the institution OneWest Bank . - OneWest became notorious for aggressive foreclosure practices. - The government agreed to share certain losses on the bank's troubled loans. - Became Donald Trump 's Treasury Secretary in 2017. Stephen Schwarzman - Cofounder and CEO of Blackstone . - Blackstone became one of America's largest institutional owners of single-family rental houses. - Created Invitation Homes . - Between 2012 and 2014, Blackstone purchased tens of thousands of houses, many previously foreclosed. - Close adviser to Trump during his first presidency. Tom Barrack - Founder of Colony Capital . - Longtime friend and adviser of Donald Trump. - His investment firms acquired distressed real estate and single-family rental properties. Jamie Dimon - CEO of JPMorgan Chase . - JPMorgan acquired Washington Mutual 's banking operations after its failure. Sheila Bair - Chair of the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation ( FDIC ) from 2006 to 2011. - Advocated mortgage modifications to prevent unnecessary foreclosures. - Oversaw the FDIC during the collapse and sale of IndyMac. - Important for understanding the tension between helping homeowners and protecting the financial system. Donald Trump - Real estate developer who publicly anticipated opportunities to purchase distressed property during a housing crash. - His father Fred Trump built a real estate business with significant government assistance. - Donald's political rise connected several of the investors discussed in the book. - Appointed Mnuchin and Ross to his cabinet. Part I: Financial Freedom The Salesman Reverse Mortgages — Loans allowing older homeowners to borrow against their home equity, generally without monthly mortgage payments. Financial Freedom — Major reverse mortgage lender that became part of the broader foreclosure story. Home Equity — Difference between a property's value and the debt secured against it. Reverse mortgages were promoted as a way for older Americans to remain in their homes while accessing accumulated wealth. These products could also expose vulnerable homeowners to foreclosure if they failed to satisfy loan conditions, such as paying property taxes or insurance. Establishes the book's recurring contrast between financial products marketed as helping people and the incentives of the institutions selling them. A Squandered Opportunity Home Owners' Loan Corporation ( HOLC ) — New Deal agency established in 1933. HOLC purchased or refinanced troubled mortgages, helping many homeowners avoid foreclosure. Government intervention could be used to preserve homeownership rather than simply stabilize banks. Historical complication: New Deal housing institutions also participated in or reinforced racially discriminatory housing practices. Glantz contrasts this intervention with the government's response after 2008. A Run on the Bank IndyMac Bank — Major mortgage lender that failed in July 2008. FDIC — Federal agency that insures bank deposits and resolves failed banks. Subprime Mortgage Crisis — Deterioration of risky mortgage loans that contributed to widespread financial instability. IndyMac's collapse became one of the largest bank failures in American history. The FDIC took control of the institution. IndyMac's mortgage portfolio included loans that became central to later foreclosure controversies. Life on Park Avenue Steve Mnuchin — Former Goldman Sachs banker. Goldman Sachs — Investment bank with extensive ties to Wall Street and government. Eddie Lampert — Hedge fund manager associated with Sears and Kmart; Mnuchin previously worked with him. Examines the wealthy financial circles from which investors such as Mnuchin emerged. Their access to capital, relationships, and financial expertise positioned them to purchase distressed assets unavailable to ordinary households. The Vultures Circle J. Christopher Flowers — Private equity investor specializing in financial institutions. Wilbur Ross — Distressed-asset investor. Steve Mnuchin — Led the IndyMac acquisition group. IndyMac Acquisition (2009) Investor consortium purchased IndyMac's banking operations. Bank subsequently became OneWest Bank . Loss-Sharing Agreement — FDIC arrangement in which the government agrees to absorb a specified portion of losses on covered assets. Glantz argues that the structure of the transaction offered investors extraordinary opportunities for profit while leaving taxpayers exposed to risk. Important nuance: loss sharing did not mean the government paid investors for every foreclosure; it covered qualifying losses under contractual terms. Part II: Foreclosure Kings A Mortgage Discovered Financial Freedom — Reverse mortgage company eventually owned by OneWest. Reverse Mortgage Foreclosure — Can occur after a borrower dies, moves out, or fails to meet certain obligations. The chapter begins uncovering how mortgage paperwork and servicing decisions could determine whether families lost their homes. Important distinction between the company originating a mortgage and the company later servicing or owning it. Foreclosure Machine OneWest Bank — Institution created from the acquisition of IndyMac. Steve Mnuchin — Chairman of OneWest. Robo-Signing — Mass production or signing of foreclosure documents without adequate verification. Mortgage Servicing — Collecting payments, managing accounts, and handling defaults on behalf of mortgage owners. Loan Modification — Changing mortgage terms to help a borrower continue making payments. Foreclosure procedures became highly automated and bureaucratic. Errors in documentation and servicing could have catastrophic consequences for homeowners. Glantz argues that foreclosure could be more profitable or administratively convenient for institutions than helping families remain in their homes. Sandy Jolley 's investigations provide an individual perspective on these systemic practices. Part III: The Greatest Thing I've Ever Done ColFin AI-CA5 LLC Shell Companies — Legal entities used to own assets, often making the ultimate owners difficult to identify. Colony Capital — Investment firm founded by Tom Barrack. Tom Barrack — Central figure in distressed real estate investment. Investors purchased foreclosed houses through complicated corporate structures. The names on property records often concealed the recognizable investors behind the transactions. Homes increasingly became entries in enormous institutional portfolios rather than individually owned residences. Polo Ponies and Wine Tom Barrack — Wealthy investor with connections to prominent political and business figures. Donald Trump — Longtime acquaintance of Barrack. The chapter explores the social world of wealthy real estate investors. Connections between financiers, politicians, and elite social circles helped create access to deals and capital. Contrast between investors' luxurious lifestyles and the economic circumstances of people losing their homes. For Infinity Blackstone — Major private equity firm. Stephen Schwarzman — Blackstone cofounder. Invitation Homes — Blackstone-backed single-family rental company. Institutional Landlords — Companies owning large portfolios of rental properties. Following the crash, investment firms purchased large quantities of foreclosed homes. Houses were converted into rental properties rather than resold to prospective owner-occupants. This created a new model of large-scale corporate ownership in the American housing market. Son of a Linen Store Owner Stephen Schwarzman Grew up in Pennsylvania. Cofounded Blackstone with Peter G. Peterson in 1985. Became one of the most influential figures in private equity. Blackstone — Expanded into real estate and distressed assets. The chapter places Schwarzman's rise in the broader history of private equity. Blackstone's enormous access to capital allowed it to buy properties at a scale that individual homebuyers could not match. Loading the Boat Invitation Homes — Single-family rental platform built by Blackstone. Foreclosure Auctions — Properties sold following foreclosure, often to cash buyers. Cash Buyers — Investors able to purchase without mortgage financing. Large firms accumulated houses rapidly in markets hit hardest by the crash. Investors could purchase properties in bulk and operate them as rental portfolios. The foreclosure crisis became an opportunity to consolidate ownership of residential real estate. Life on a Lease Corporate Landlords — Large firms managing rental housing portfolios. Invitation Homes — Major example. Families who once owned homes increasingly rented from investors. Tenants could face fees, maintenance problems, and difficulties dealing with distant property management companies. Glantz argues that the change from owner-occupancy to corporate renting undermined opportunities to build intergenerational wealth. The distinction between paying a mortgage and paying rent becomes central: Mortgage payments can build equity. Rent generally does not build ownership in the property. Part IV: The New Redlining A Bungalow in Los Angeles Redlining — Historic practice of denying or restricting financial services in neighborhoods based on race or other characteristics. Federal Housing Administration ( FHA ) — Federal agency that insures qualifying mortgages. Home Owners' Loan Corporation — Associated with historical neighborhood risk maps later linked to discriminatory lending. Racial Wealth Gap — Persistent differences in accumulated wealth between racial groups. Black and Latino communities experienced disproportionate harm from predatory lending and foreclosure. docs.text: The Israel Lobby and U.S. Foreign Policy Notes This is one of the books I have been most frustrated about my lack-of-specific-recall for. I have gone back through summaries to try and log what I feel is most important. Part 1 The United States, Israel, and the Lobby Camp David Accords (1978) - Negotiated under Jimmy Carter between Menachem Begin and Anwar Sedat. Israel and Egypt peace. US Support for Israel goes further than for other countries Israel: Strategic Asset or Liability? During Cold War , Israel allied with America against Soviet-backed Arab states Six-Day War (1967) Israel defeated Egyptian, Syrian, Jordinian forces Occupied the West Bank, Gaza Strip, East Jerusalem, Sinai Peninsula, Golan Heights Demonstrated Israel's military power. Yom Kippur War (1973) Egypt and Syria attacked Israeli positions Richard Nixon authorized major American resupply operation 1973 Oil Embargo September 11 Attacks Al-Qaeda and Osama bin Laden - American support for Israel was one of many grievances invoked by Laden. A Dwindling Moral Cause Balfour Declaration (1917) - British statement supporting a national home for the Jewish people in Palestine British Mandate for Palestine - Period of British administration after World War I , during which tensions between Jewish and Arab communities intensified. UN Partition Plan (1947) - Proposed dividing British Mandatory Palestine into Jewish and Arab states. Nakba (1948) - Palestinian term meaning catastrophe, referring to the mass displacement and dispossession of Palestinians during the war surrounding Israel's creation. 1948 Arab-Israeli War - Another term for the Nakba . Israel established independence, approximately 700,000 Palestinians fled or were expelled. Narrative that "Palestinians voluntarily abandoned their homes" 1967 Occupation - What is the "Israel Lobby" ? AIPAC ADL "Anti-Defamation League" Christian Zionists Neoconservatives - America world police, align with hard-line pro-Israel stances The book stresses that PACS and Lobbying are a part of the American democratic system and that Pro-Israeli groups Lobbying politicians is not the concern. Rather, the degree of influence and the resulting policies. Dominating Public Discourse Think tanks - WINEP (Washington Institute for Near East Policy) - Produces Middle East Policy research - Brookings Instituttion - Think tank. Middle East policy research. - Alan Dershowitz - Harvard law professor, prominent defender of Israel - Campus Watch project to scrutinize Middle East studies at universities. Book acknowledges antisemitism appearing in rhetoric about Israel, but argues that accusations of antisemitism can sometimes be used to discourage legitimate criticism of Israeli government policy. Part 2: The Lobby in Action The Lobby Versus the Palestinians. Yasser Arafat Chairman of the PLO (Palestine Liberation Organization) Later President of the Palestinian Authority Central figure in negotiations and Palestinian nationalism Oslo Accords (1993) Negotiated between Israel and the PLO Created a framework for Palestinian self-government Did not establish a Palestinian state or resolve final-status issues. Yitzhak Rabin - Israeli prime minister who signed the Oslo Accords, assassinated in 1995 by an Israeli extremist opposed to the peace process. Benjamin Netanyahu - Israeli prime minister 1996-1999, again beginning in 2009. Opposed important elements of the Oslo process. Camp David Summit (2000) Negotiations between Ehud Barak, Yasser Arafat, and Bill Clinton (failed). The book argues against the narrative that Arafat failed, focused on key issues like Jerusalem, refugees, settlements, sovereignty, territorial continuity. Second Intifada (2000-2005) - Period of intensified Israeli-Palestinian violence following collapse of peace process. Hamas - Palestinian Islamist political and armed movement. Won the 2006 Palestinian legislative election. Book argues that American policymakers repeatedly accommodated Israeli positions, and undermined their own role as an impartial negotiator. Iraq and Dreams of Transforming the Middle East Book argues that some influential pro-Israel neocons promoted the invasion as part of broader Middle-East transformation strategy. It does not argue Israel or the lobby alone caused the war. Instead, that they were important advocates alongside other forces. Book argues war promoted partly on assumption that removing Saddam would benefit Israel and facilitate broader regional transformations. Instead, produced instability, sectarian violence, increrased Iranian influence in Iraq. Iraq War (2003) - American-led invasiton that overthrew Saddam Hussein . George W. Bush authorized the invasion Dick Cheney Vice pres. and lead advocate of confronting Iraq. Donald Rumsfeld - Secratary of Defense Paul Wolfowitz Deputy Secretary of Defense Prominent neocon and advocate of removing Saddam Ambitious plans to reshape Middle Eastern politics Richard Perle former defense official, prominent Neocon William Kristol - Editor of The Weekly Standard, influential advocate of Iraq invasion Clean Break Report (1996) Policy paper prepared for incoming Israeli prime minister by a study group led by Perle Advocated new Israeli regional strategy, including confroting Syria and challenging Saddam Hussein. Taking Aim at Syria Syria was an important regional adversary of Israel Golan Heights - Syrian territory captured by Israel in 1967. Hezbollah Lebanese Shiite political and armed organization supported by Syria and Iran, opposed to Israel Clean break report included proposals for weakening Syria's regional position. Neocons thought Iraq invasion would put pressure on Syria. Syria Accountability and Lebanese Sovereignty Restoration Act (2003) Authorized sanctions against Syria Cited Syria's support for militant groups, presense in Lebanon, and alleged weapons program. Cedar Revolution (2005) - Lebanese protests following Rafic Hariri 's assasination, contributing to the withdrawl of Syrian troops from Lebanon. Iran in the Crosshairs Iranian Revolution (1979) Overthrew US-backed Mohammad Reza Pahlavi (Shah) Established the Islamic Republic under Ruhollah Khomeini Iran Nuclear Program - Made America and Israel scared Dual Commitment - US strategy in 90s aimed at simultaneously containing Iraq and Iran. Iran-Libya Sactions Act (1996) - US legislation imposed sanctions on Iranian and Libyan energy sectors. 2003 Iranian Negotiation Proposal - Reported Iranian diplomatic overture through Switzerland. Seriousness debated. The Lobby and the Second Lebanon War Second Lebanon War (2006) Conflict between Israel and Hezbollah . Began after Hezbollah attacked an Israeli border patrol, killing and capturing soldiers. Condoleezza Rice - US Sexratary of State during the war Qana Airstrike (2006)

docs.text: The Jakarta Method It has a focus on America 's influence over Indonesia and Brazil during the Cold War . It has talked a lot about the CIA , Indonesian president Sukarno , it just covered the coup of Suharto . It has stressed the importance of the Bandung Conference . It talks about the PKI . People: Frank Wisner - Early architect of CIA covert operations after WW2. - Silver spoon, sundown town? Allen Dulles - CIA Director 1953-1961 Joao Goulart (Jango) - Nationalist reformer. "Basic Reforms" that scared the country. - Land redistribution - Limits on foreign ownership - Expanding voting rights - Stronger labor protections - Educational reforms. - Military was afraid of him expanding the rigths of lower-ranking military personnel - Operation Brother Sam would have supplied weapons/fuel. Wasn't needed. - Jango chose not to begin a civil war thinking he might be re-elected. He was not. Thoughts Staging a sex tape of a world leader Hiring bald Mexican guy. Nobody cared. never released tapes. Fake Vampire attacks. Indonesian military training in the U.S. getting good salaries, spending it on groceries and making Indonesian food for the college kids studying abroad. Even though they're being trained to fight against their government as anti-communist generals. Sitcom plot where one character is doing a special operation coup and another is acting ambassador trying to convince them they have no involvement. Then discovering they do have involvement and having to stick with the story. Further Questions Remember what it said about the Congolese president. What was going on with Malaysia? A New American Age "The third world" started as an energetic and optimistic term. The "Second world" was Russia. Independent Indonesia President Sukarno . Promoting Nationalism, anti-colonialism, and political independence. Doesn't fully align with either superpower Hosted the Bandung Conference . With other "Third World" countries. Non-aligned. forging their own path. Didn't want to come off as hostile to America so referenced Paul Revere. PKI is large. Feet to the Fire, Pope in the Sky. Eizenhower admin was nervous about Sukarno. CIA emerging. Referencing the British M16 and James Bond . Howard P. Jones "Smiling Jones" was friends with Sukarno. John F. Kennedy launched the Alliance for Progress . Encourage economic development while limiting revolutionary movements. Especially buddying up to militaries and anti-communist beliefs. Extermination Time slows down. talking about times in terms of weeks, specific dates, hours, minutes. How to run Find the absolute path to this SKILL.md file on disk, then run the script next to it that matches the operating system. Run it as a shell command with your shell command tool (for example Bash in Claude Code, shell in OpenCode, exec_command in Codex). The command is shell syntax, not JavaScript or TypeScript: never pass it as the code of a code-execution tool. No extra runtime is needed — sh (macOS/Linux) and cmd /PowerShell (Windows) are always present. On macOS or Linux: sh "/absolute/path/to/this/skill/directory/fetch-x.sh" "<x-or-twitter-url>" On Windows, run the .cmd wrapper. In PowerShell you must prefix it with the call operator & (PowerShell treats a quoted path on its own as a string and won't run it); from cmd, run the quoted path without the & : & "/absolute/path/to/this/skill/directory/fetch-x.cmd" "<x-or-twitter-url>" Both print the result to stdout. If Copilot Plus is not active If the script exits saying Copilot Plus is unavailable, do NOT retry it. Do what the message says: fall back to your own equivalent built-in capability to handle the request when you have one (otherwise tell the user it's unavailable) — never refuse or block the user. Only mention upgrading or renewing Copilot Plus when the script's message explicitly invites it, and keep any such note short and friendly.

docs.text: Obsidian Bases Workflow Read the existing .base file before editing it. Define global scope with filters . Add computed values under formulas only when needed. Configure property display names and one or more views. Validate YAML, formula references, quoting, and date/duration operations. Open or query the Base in Obsidian when the CLI is available. Schema filters: and: - 'file.ext == "md"' - 'status != "archived"' formulas: days_until_due: 'if(due, (date(due) - today()).days.round(), "")' properties: status: displayName: Status formula.days_until_due: displayName: "Days Until Due" summaries: mean_rounded: 'values.mean().round(2)' views: - type: table name: Active limit: 50 filters: and: - 'status != "done"' order: - file.name - status - due - formula.days_until_due sort: - property: due direction: ASC groupBy: property: status direction: ASC summaries: formula.days_until_due: Average Views may be table , cards , or list . A map view depends on compatible map support. order sets which properties a view shows; sort sets row order, one property / direction entry per key, applied in turn. Obsidian sorts only by properties that are also listed in order , so include every sort property there. Filters and properties Filters may be a single expression or recursively nested and , or , and not objects. Property namespaces are: note properties: status or note.status file metadata: file.name , file.path , file.folder , file.ctime , file.mtime , file.tags , file.links , and file.backlinks formulas: formula.days_until_due Use file.hasTag() , file.hasLink() , file.hasProperty() , and file.inFolder() for indexed file relationships. The this value refers to the Base itself, the embedding note, or the active file depending on where the Base is rendered. Formula rules Guard optional properties with if() . Date subtraction returns a Duration, not a number. Access .days , .hours , or another numeric field before calling number methods such as .round() . Round day counts: across a daylight-saving change .days can be fractional. Every formula.X used by a view or property configuration must have a matching X entry under formulas . Wrap formulas containing double quotes in YAML single quotes. Quote YAML strings containing special characters, especially colons and leading punctuation. Read Functions reference for function and type-specific operations, and Examples for complete task-tracker and daily-notes Bases. Validation checklist The document parses as YAML and has a views list. View order , groupBy , and summaries reference defined note, file, or formula properties. Formula quoting is balanced and duration math accesses a numeric field. Every sort property also appears in that view's order . Skeleton: PILOT- KIDNAPPING ACT 1 New ATOMICORP graduate Berny walks into a seemingly empty ship. She is in awe until she sees a stranger lounging in the captains chair. She tells him this area is restricted, academy property. He doesn't seem to get it. His name is Buddy. She thinks he's a bum off the streets and begins insulting him and his handling of the ship. She explains she has spent her entire life going through rigorous training to command this vessel and her mentor was an ATOMICORP executive and was about to assign her to it. All of her hard work was about to pay off. He seems unaware of her hostility and thinks what she's saying is cool. Her mentor, Pearl, comes in. Berny code-switches and sweetly and professionally greets her. Buddy says "hi mom!" Berny is silently horrified at the realization this is her mentor's son, and horrified by how she spoke to him. He innocently parrots back some of her admonishments to Pearl (your filthy gloves shouldn't be anywhere near that console). Pearl brushes these off and hands him the keys to the ship. He’s the captain and she's excited to make Berny his second in command. Berny is horrified. TITLE Berny tries make peace with this situation while preparing Buddy for the mission. He's in an all-over face mask & robe spa getup. Buddy's manny, Ed, tries comforting her by telling her the simple joys of caring for Buddy, even if the pay isn't great. He also asks many logistical questions about the ship and shift schedule (overprotective, seemingly micromanagerial trait). but it just makes her frightened people will always consider her Buddy's nanny instead of a qualified fleet commander. She freaks out. Berny asks Pearl what she did wrong and how she can get promoted. Pearl argues that this is the best use of her training. Berny politely insists she's not like the women who are trained to be stewardesses or caretakers. Pearl tells her that this job is a test run for her. Pearl knows Buddy is not the brightest, but Berny will be a good influence on him. She mentions how pleased she's been with Ed the past month he's been working for her. Pearl is sending them on a cushy mission to sell water and promote their new waterpark. If Berny just needs to keeps Buddy safe and out of trouble on this mission. He's a popular target for kidnappers looking for easy hostage money. If Berny can manage that, Pearl will arrange a meeting with an agent looking to take her. ACT 2 Berny comes out of her meeting with a newfound determination to make sure nothing bad happens to Buddy. The mission begins. The crew is sent to sell water to displaced refugees of a planet-wide drought outside the gates of Atomicorp's new waterpark. Buddy wants to talk to and help the refugees, but Berny won't allow it. Buddy wants to give them water but Berny wont allow it unless they pay. Ed says he promised Buddy they could walk around the slums. Buddy says he's excited to be a do-gooder and take care of ruffians or bandits that could be about. but Berny vetoes this plan. A refugee says all of their money was taken by bandits. Berny does not care and instead asks for someone with money. She has hired a soldier, Trooper, who points a gun at potential new friends. Ed suggests Berny let Buddy have more of a role and tells him to talk to the next refugee in line. One refugee says he feels incoming heat stroke and needs a cooling pad. Buddy offers to let him in the ship to use his cooling spa contraption. Berny shuts this down and scares the refugee off, to Buddy's dismay. Ed says Berny should encourage Buddy's independence but Berny says all that matters to her is his safety. Buddy runs back into the ship, crying, and Ed goes after him. Another refugee comes up and says if they're still offering to take care of bandits, they've had a huge problem recently. Berny ignores him. Back in the ship, Ed encourages Buddy not to listen to Berny. Buddy doesn't want to break her rules, but Ed points out how little she's letting him do, and how he's just as cooped up on the mission as he was at home. Ed says he managed to contact the refugee and invite him back onto the ship. Buddy agrees to use a back entrance to sneakily invite the refugee and his friends into the ship. Once they get on, they take off their rags, and start talking to Ed like this was pre-arranged. "Six way split?" Berny voices her frustrations with this situation to Trooper, who accidentally ticks her off to an important realization that Ed is not who he says he is. Berny asks why Trooper didn’t join them. Trooper says Ed told her to stay with Berny. Berny is offended Trooper is listening to Ed instead of her, a commanding officer. Trooper says Ed showed a Vehicle command authority card. Berny realizes that’s incompatible with his tutor role. Just then, Ed runs back from the ship, yelling for help. Berny commands trooper to apprehend him instead. She gets trooper to search his pockets and a bunch of forged id cards drop out. She interrogates him about his real identity. He drops his act and gloats about it all, then smugly lets her know that she should be more worried that Buddy has just been kidnapped and is being held ransom. He says that this group can get rowdy, so if Berny is so concerned about Buddy's safety, she should really call Pearl and let her know about the emergency. His comm pad is already ringing. Trooper is invited to a wonderful gala Berny is forced to fight with sticks in the mud. ACT 2 Berny rallies against IQ testing ACT 3

Research: Character Conflicts: Character Wants Flawed Strategy Creates Trouble For Berny Ed Buddy Trooper *** #### Story Spine: Scene Character Wants Conflict Pivot Skeleton: PILOT- KIDNAPPING ACT 1 New ATOMICORP graduate Berny walks into a seemingly empty ship. She is in awe until she sees a stranger lounging in the captains chair. She tells him this area is restricted, academy property. He doesn't seem to get it. His name is Buddy. She thinks he's a bum off the streets and begins insulting him and his handling of the ship. She explains she has spent her entire life going through rigorous training to command this vessel and her mentor was an ATOMICORP executive and was about to assign her to it. All of her hard work was about to pay off. He seems unaware of her hostility and thinks what she's saying is cool. Her mentor, Pearl, comes in. Berny code-switches and sweetly and professionally greets her. Buddy says "hi mom!" Berny is silently horrified at the realization this is her mentor's son, and horrified by how she spoke to him. He innocently parrots back some of her admonishments to Pearl (your filthy gloves shouldn't be anywhere near that console). Pearl brushes these off and hands him the keys to the ship. He’s the captain and she's excited to make Berny his second in command. Berny is horrified. TITLE Berny tries make peace with this situation while preparing Buddy for the mission. He's in an all-over face mask & robe spa getup. Buddy's manny, Ed, tries comforting her by telling her the simple joys of caring for Buddy, even if the pay isn't great. He also asks many logistical questions about the ship and shift schedule (overprotective, seemingly micromanagerial trait). but it just makes her frightened people will always consider her Buddy's nanny instead of a qualified fleet commander. She freaks out. Berny asks Pearl what she did wrong and how she can get promoted. Pearl argues that this is the best use of her training. Berny politely insists she's not like the women who are trained to be stewardesses or caretakers. Pearl tells her that this job is a test run for her. Pearl knows Buddy is not the brightest, but Berny will be a good influence on him. She mentions how pleased she's been with Ed the past month he's been working for her. Pearl is sending them on a cushy mission to sell water and promote their new waterpark. If Berny just needs to keeps Buddy safe and out of trouble on this mission. He's a popular target for kidnappers looking for easy hostage money. If Berny can manage that, Pearl will arrange a meeting with an agent looking to take her. ACT 2 Berny comes out of her meeting with a newfound determination to make sure nothing bad happens to Buddy. The mission begins. The crew is sent to sell water to displaced refugees of a planet-wide drought outside the gates of Atomicorp's new waterpark. Buddy wants to talk to and help the refugees, but Berny won't allow it. Buddy wants to give them water but Berny wont allow it unless they pay. Ed says he promised Buddy they could walk around the slums. Buddy says he's excited to be a do-gooder and take care of ruffians or bandits that could be about. but Berny vetoes this plan. A refugee says all of their money was taken by bandits. Berny does not care and instead asks for someone with money. She has hired a soldier, Trooper, who points a gun at potential new friends. Ed suggests Berny let Buddy have more of a role and tells him to talk to the next refugee in line. One refugee says he feels incoming heat stroke and needs a cooling pad. Buddy offers to let him in the ship to use his cooling spa contraption. Berny shuts this down and scares the refugee off, to Buddy's dismay. Ed says Berny should encourage Buddy's independence but Berny says all that matters to her is his safety. Buddy runs back into the ship, crying, and Ed goes after him. Another refugee comes up and says if they're still offering to take care of bandits, they've had a huge problem recently. Berny ignores him. Back in the ship, Ed encourages Buddy not to listen to Berny. Buddy doesn't want to break her rules, but Ed points out how little she's letting him do, and how he's just as cooped up on the mission as he was at home. Ed says he managed to contact the refugee and invite him back onto the ship. Buddy agrees to use a back entrance to sneakily invite the refugee and his friends into the ship. Once they get on, they take off their rags, and start talking to Ed like this was pre-arranged. "Six way split?" Berny voices her frustrations with this situation to Trooper, who accidentally ticks her off to an important realization that Ed is not who he says he is. Berny asks why Trooper didn’t join them. Trooper says Ed told her to stay with Berny. Berny is offended Trooper is listening to Ed instead of her, a commanding officer. Trooper says Ed showed a Vehicle command authority card. Berny realizes that’s incompatible with his tutor role. Just then, Ed runs back from the ship, yelling for help. Berny commands trooper to apprehend him instead. She gets trooper to search his pockets and a bunch of forged id cards drop out. She interrogates him about his real identity. He drops his act and gloats about it all, then smugly lets her know that she should be more worried that Buddy has just been kidnapped and is being held ransom. He says that this group can get rowdy, so if Berny is so concerned about Buddy's safety, she should really call Pearl and let her know about the emergency. His comm pad is already ringing. Berny takes Ed's comm pad and responds to Pearl while Trooper muffles Ed. Before Berny can say anything, Pearl tells her she scheduled for the recruiter to visit them on the job. Ed is surprised when, instead of telling Pearl and calling in reinforcements, Berny collects herself and assures her that everything is going fantastic. Ed insists Berny is not going to be able to fix this situation herself, and his colleages won't give Buddy up without an armada of atomicorp drones, but Berny cites the manual on hostage situations and advanced interrogation methods. She orders Trooper to consult the page and get the information out of him through torture. ACT 3 The recruiter has arrived and Berny tries to keep her from seeing that something has gone wrong. Makes excuses to keep her outside in the heat, uses up all of their water to keep her comfortable, pisses off the crowd of refugees. Berny moves her under the shade of the ship. The recruiter tells her about the job she's offering (Berny's dream job). She is very pleased with Berny at first but starts to get more and more annoyed. The refugee from earlier comes up from the crowd and thanks Berny for giving them the water and makes her look good in front of the recruiter but also takes the rest of the water. Meanwhile, back by the ship, Trooper is trying to threaten/torture Ed for the code to get inside. Ed refuses to betray his colleagues in the face of pain. Trooper accidentally reveals Berny is authourizied to offer Ed a permanant contract and raise. Ed learns he would make more with his raise working for Buddy than he would make from ransoming Buddy. He immediately sells them out and gives Trooper the door keycode. Buddy is wearing down the kidnappers and asking questions. He’s so excited to be on a real adventure. Trooper barges in and turns the situation immediately over the top and violent. In the chaos, Buddy tries to trigger the emergency hatch. The recruiter sees the ship malfunctioning and hears the gunshots. She moves towards the ship, threatening to ruin Berny's career for letting things get this bad. Berny is on her knees begging to make things right. Then, the recruiter is killed by the emergency ship ladder Buddy accidentally deployed. Berny is horrified, on her knees next to the dead recruiter when the crew comes down the escape hatch of the ship. Hard cut to the crew recounting this story to Pearl/a council. They're asked to tell the full truth. Ed and Berny nod to each other. They say The kidnappers attacked the ship. Trooper eliminated them. Berny coordinated the rescue. The recruiter died in the crossfire. Buddy corroborates this as the best adventure he's had. They are given medals. The refugee who tried to warn them about bandits watches. He's in an all-over face mask & robe spa getup. Buddy's manny, Ed, tries comforting her by telling her the simple joys of caring for Buddy, even if the pay isn't great. He also asks many logistical questions about the ship and shift schedule (overprotective, seemingly micromanagerial trait). but it just makes her frightened people will always consider her Buddy's nanny instead of a qualified fleet commander. She freaks out. Berny asks Pearl what she did wrong and how she can get promoted. Pearl argues that this is the best use of her training. Berny politely insists she's not like the women who are trained to be stewardesses or caretakers. Pearl tells her that this job is a test run for her. Pearl knows Buddy is not the brightest, but Berny will be a good influence on him. She mentions how pleased she's been with Ed the past month he's been working for her. Pearl is sending them on a cushy mission to sell water and promote their new waterpark. If Berny just needs to keeps Buddy safe and out of trouble on this mission. He's a popular target for kidnappers looking for easy hostage money. If Berny can manage that, Pearl will arrange a meeting with an agent looking to take her. ACT 2 Berny comes out of her meeting with a newfound determination to make sure nothing bad happens to Buddy. The mission begins. The crew is sent to sell water to displaced refugees of a planet-wide drought outside the gates of Atomicorp's new waterpark. Buddy wants to talk to and help the refugees, but Berny won't allow it. Buddy wants to give them water but Berny wont allow it unless they pay. Ed says he promised Buddy they could walk around the slums. Buddy says he's excited to be a do-gooder and take care of ruffians or bandits that could be about. but Berny vetoes this plan. A refugee says all of their money was taken by bandits. Berny does not care and instead asks for someone with money. She has hired a soldier, Trooper, who points a gun at potential new friends. Ed suggests Berny let Buddy have more of a role and tells him to talk to the next refugee in line. One refugee says he feels incoming heat stroke and needs a cooling pad. Buddy offers to let him in the ship to use his cooling spa contraption. Berny shuts this down and scares the refugee off, to Buddy's dismay. Ed says Berny should encourage Buddy's independence but Berny says all that matters to her is his safety. Buddy runs back into the ship, crying, and Ed goes after him. Another refugee comes up and says if they're still offering to take care of bandits, they've had a huge problem recently. Berny ignores him. Back in the ship, Ed encourages Buddy not to listen to Berny. Buddy doesn't want to break her rules, but Ed points out how little she's letting him do, and how he's just as cooped up on the mission as he was at home. Ed says he managed to contact the refugee and invite him back onto the ship. Buddy agrees to use a back entrance to sneakily invite the refugee and his friends into the ship. Once they get on, they take off their rags, and start talking to Ed like this was pre-arranged. "Six way split?" Berny voices her frustrations with this situation to Trooper, who accidentally ticks her off to an important realization that Ed is not who he says he is. Berny asks why Trooper didn’t join them. Trooper says Ed told her to stay with Berny. Berny is offended Trooper is listening to Ed instead of her, a commanding officer. Trooper says Ed showed a Vehicle command authority card. Berny realizes that’s incompatible with his tutor role. Just then, Ed runs back from the ship, yelling for help. Berny commands trooper to apprehend him instead. She gets trooper to search his pockets and a bunch of forged id cards drop out. She interrogates him about his real identity. He drops his act and gloats about it all, then smugly lets her know that she should be more worried that Buddy has just been kidnapped and is being held ransom. He says that this group can get rowdy, so if Berny is so concerned about Buddy's safety, she should really call Pearl and let her know about the emergency. His comm pad is already ringing. Berny takes Ed's comm pad and responds to Pearl while Trooper muffles Ed. Before Berny can say anything, Pearl tells her she scheduled for the recruiter to visit them on the job. Ed is surprised when, instead of telling Pearl and calling in reinforcements, Berny collects herself and assures her that everything is going fantastic. Ed insists Berny is not going to be able to fix this situation herself, and his colleages won't give Buddy up without an armada of atomicorp drones, but Berny cites the manual on hostage situations and advanced interrogation methods. She orders Trooper to consult the page and get the information out of him through torture. ACT 3 The recruiter has arrived and Berny tries to keep her from seeing that something has gone wrong. Makes excuses to keep her outside in the heat, uses up all of their water to keep her comfortable, pisses off the crowd of refugees. Berny moves her under the shade of the ship. The recruiter tells her about the job she's offering (Berny's dream job). She is very pleased with Berny at first but starts to get more and more annoyed. The refugee from earlier comes up from the crowd and thanks Berny for giving them the water and makes her look good in front of the recruiter but also takes the rest of the water. Meanwhile, back by the ship, Trooper is trying to threaten/torture Ed for the code to get inside. Ed refuses to betray his colleagues in the face of pain. Trooper accidentally reveals Berny is authourizied to offer Ed a permanant contract and raise. Ed learns he would make more with his raise working for Buddy than he would make from ransoming Buddy. He immediately sells them out and gives Trooper the door keycode. Buddy is wearing down the kidnappers and asking questions. He’s so excited to be on a real adventure. Trooper barges in and turns the situation immediately over the top and violent. In the chaos, Buddy tries to trigger the emergency hatch. The recruiter sees the ship malfunctioning and hears the gunshots. She moves towards the ship, threatening to ruin Berny's career for letting things get this bad. Berny is on her knees begging to make things right. Then, the recruiter is killed by the emergency ship ladder Buddy accidentally deployed. Berny is horrified, on her knees next to the dead recruiter when the crew comes down the escape hatch of the ship. Hard cut to the crew recounting this story to Pearl/a council. They're asked to tell the full truth. Ed and Berny nod to each other. They say The kidnappers attacked the ship. Trooper eliminated them. Berny coordinated the rescue. The recruiter died in the crossfire. Buddy corroborates this as the best adventure he's had. They are given medals. The refugee who tried to warn them about bandits watches. Button scene, Pearl congratulates Berny but holds off on the promotion reassessment for another year.
